clicks:
1. Sign in as the HR lead (demo.hr@example.com).
2. In the left menu, click “People”.
3. In the hub’s icon strip, choose “Assets” (point at the icons to see their names).
4. Use the “Physical” and “Digital” chips above the table to split the register.
5. Click the search bar at the top of the screen (or press Ctrl+K / ⌘K), type “Asset categories” and choose “Asset categories”. to see the 10 ready-made categories and which kind each one is.
comments: Every category is marked Physical (laptop, phone, SIM card, ID card, company card, monitor) or Digital (email account, system login, software licence, phone number). HR can add more categories, e.g. a separate one for Zoho logins.

clicks:
1. Sign in as the HR lead (demo.hr@example.com).
2. In the left menu, click “People”.
3. In the hub’s icon strip, choose “Assets” (point at the icons to see their names).
4. Stay on “The register”. Each row shows the item, category, status, who has it (“With”), country and cost.
5. Use the country box (“Every country”), the status chips and the search box to narrow the list.
6. Press “Export” to download the whole register as an Excel file.
comments: One register for every country the user can see. The demo has only one item (a spare laptop, VN-LT-00007), so add a few with “Add an item” to see it fill up. Sorting by column is done in the downloaded Excel file (it opens with filters on); the screen itself filters but does not sort by column.

clicks:
1. Sign in as the HR lead (demo.hr@example.com).
2. In the left menu, click “People”.
3. In the hub’s icon strip, choose “Assets” (point at the icons to see their names).
4. Press “Requests” in the segment bar. Requests raised automatically for joiners appear here (for example the one for Ly Thi Thu) with a suggested spare.
5. To hand something over: open an item on “The register”, press “Give to someone”, pick the person and write the condition it goes out in.
6. Open the item again: the drawer shows make and model, cost, invoice, warranty end and “Who has had it” with the date it was given.
7. Sign in as the employee and go to payobook.com/my, then open “My Things”. The item is listed with a “Yes, I have it” button.
comments: When a joiner’s onboarding checklist opens, a laptop request is raised by itself and the laptop step is given to the person who arranges it. Only the laptop is raised automatically today; other items (ID card, email, etc.) are added by hand. The employee sees their items on their own “My Things” page; the HR employee record has no assets tab yet (HR uses the register’s search instead).

clicks:
1. Sign in as the HR lead (demo.hr@example.com).
2. In the left menu, click “People”.
3. In the hub’s icon strip, choose “Assets” (point at the icons to see their names).
4. On “The register”, click an item that is with someone.

clicks:
1. Sign in as the HR lead (demo.hr@example.com).
2. In the left menu, click “People”.
3. In the hub’s icon strip, choose “Assets” (point at the icons to see their names).
4. Press “Add an item”, fill in what it is, the category and the country, and save.
5. The new row gets its own code, e.g. VN-LT-00008 (country – category – number). Click it to see its full history.
comments: Codes are made automatically per country and category, for physical and digital items alike, and never reused. The history stays with the code for the item’s whole life.

clicks:
1. Sign in as the HR lead (demo.hr@example.com).
2. In the left menu, click “People”.
3. In the hub’s icon strip, choose “Assets” (point at the icons to see their names).
4. Read the numbers at the top: “Items on the books”, “Out with people”, “Spare in the cupboard”, “Under repair”, “Accounts live”, “Leavers still holding”.
5. Use the status chips (Spare, Assigned, Under repair, To scrap, Scrapped) and the country box to count by country.
6. To change a status, open an item and press the status button in the drawer, or tick several rows and press “Change status”.
comments: Statuses are Spare / Assigned / Under repair / To scrap / Scrapped (and Available / Active / Switched off for digital items). Warranty end is shown on each item, with a warning when it is ending.

clicks:
1. Sign in as the HR lead (demo.hr@example.com).
2. In the left menu, click “People”.
3. In the hub’s icon strip, choose “Assets” (point at the icons to see their names).
4. Press “Add an item”, choose a digital category such as “Email account” or “System login”, put the address in “Serial number or address”, and give it to someone.
5. Click the “Digital” chip to see every account and its status (Available / Active / Switched off).
6. When that person leaves and their leaving checklist opens (left menu “Lifecycle”, hub icon “Exits”), a step “Switch off: …” is added for each of their accounts.
7. The employee sees their accounts on payobook.com/my under “My Things”.
comments: Digital items are tracked like physical ones, with Active and Switched off instead of handed back. The switch-off step is added to the leaving checklist automatically; the account itself is switched off by IT in the other system.

clicks:
1. Sign in as the HR lead (demo.hr@example.com).
2. In the left menu, click “Lifecycle”, then choose “Exits” in the hub’s icon strip.
3. Open a leaver’s checklist: there is a “Return: …” step for each physical item they still hold.
4. To take an item back, go to “People” › “Assets”, open the item and press “Take it back”; write the condition it came back in. The return date is recorded.
5. Until every “Return: …” step is done, the final settlement for that person is held.
comments: Returns are mandatory: open returns hold the final settlement, and the return date and condition are recorded. There is no separate sign-off on each return — ticking the step and taking the item back is the record.

clicks:

4. Press “Add an item” and fill in Country, Cost (in the local currency) and “Where it can go”.
5. Open the item: the drawer shows the country and the cost in local currency with the US dollar amount beside it.
comments: Country tag, local currency and the US dollar figure are built. “Where it can go” is a written note only — the system does not stop an item being moved to another country.

clicks:

clicks:
